messages.subject: Conditional QTL mapping
messages.body_plain:
Dear Dr. Broman,

Is there a way to calculate conditional trait values followed by conditional QTL mapping in R/qtl?

Specifically, I want to see the effect of Trait 1 conditional on another Trait 2 (T1|T2), so that the phenotypic values of Trait 1 are the net trait values which are independent of variation in Trait 2. This is to understand the genetic basis (pleiotropy/tight linkage) of colocalised QTL for Trait 1 and Trait 2.

Any comments, thoughts or suggestions would be greatly appreciated.
Thanks,
Shikha

messages.subject: Re: Conditional QTL mapping
messages.body_plain:
This is not included in R/qtl. But you could use the R function lm() to fit the regression of trait 1 on trait 2, and the residuals.

karl

messages.subject: When we have to use covariate or not for QTL analysis?
messages.subject_clean: When we have to use covariate or not for QTL analysis?
messages.body_plain:
Dear Dr. Karl,

I have one trait (phenotype) and around ~1000 genotype data. I would like to make QTL analysis. However, I fell a little bit confused when I use covariate or not? I read about this on https://rqtl.org/tutorials/rqtltour.pdf However, I am still confused. How to get the data "fake.bc" or listeria in excel or .csv format?
Could you please help me?
I appreciate your help!

Best,
Amirandi

messages.subject: Re: When we have to use covariate or not for QTL analysis?
messages.subject_clean: When we have to use covariate or not for QTL analysis?
messages.body_plain:
The use of covariates is discussed in Chapter 7 of the R/qtl book (https://rqtl.org/book). "If a covariate has a large effect on the phenotype, its inclusion in the analysis will result in reduced residual variation and so will enhance our ability to detect QTL. It is also of interest to assess possible QTL × covariate interactions. For example, does a QTL have different effects in the two sexes?"

The fake.bc and listeria datasets are distributed with R/qtl. You can load them with data() and write them to a file with write.cross().
The listeria data is also provided in several formats at https://rqtl.org/sampledata

karl
